props.gloss_en: 'and when you walk on the way' -- to the exclusion of a groom
from here they said: one who marries a virgin is exempt [from the Shema]
and one who marries a widow is obligated
Rav Pappa: like 'the way' -- as the way is voluntary, so here too [the obligation is in what is] voluntary
if so, let the verse say 'when walking'; what is 'when YOU walk'? conclude from it: in your own walking you are obligated, in that of a mitzva you are exempt
here [one marrying a virgin] is preoccupied, here [one marrying a widow] is not
Rav: a mourner is obligated in all the mitzvot said in the Torah
for 'splendour' is said of them, as it is said: 'bind your splendour upon you' (Ezek 24:17)
there it is a preoccupation of the voluntary; here, a preoccupation of a mitzva

objections.gloss_en: מי לא עסקינן דקאזיל לדבר מצוה, ואפילו הכי אמר רחמנא ליקרי -- does the verse's 'way' not include one walking for a mitzva, whom the Torah still tells to recite?

objections.gloss_en: אי הכי מאי איריא הכונס את הבתולה? אפילו כונס את האלמנה נמי -- if a mitzva exempts, one marrying a widow should be exempt too; yet the baraita obligates him

answered_by.gloss_en: הכא טריד, והכא לא טריד (= p_tarid)
